title: Owens River Photoshop workflow: sky extension, layer separation, and painting light

summary: This video presents a practitioner’s in-depth Photoshop-based workflow to build a three-dimensional landscape image from a low-contrast, twilight-like scene. Working from the Owens River subject, the instructor demonstrates segmentation of the image into sky, mountains, and foreground, then expands the sky, adds haze to create depth, and repeatedly shifts between raw processing and painted light to simulate a directional leftward illumination. Central themes include a heavy emphasis on separating layers to control depth, painting light rather than relying solely on captured light, and using techniques such as blur plus luminosity, color grading, and 50-150 adjustments to exaggerate and refine tonal relationships. The progression moves from initial toning and cropping to aggressive sky and mid-ground edits, culminating in final touches that restore balance between foreground, mid-ground, and background components while preserving three-dimensionality.

sections.title: Scene setup and zone planning
concepts: sky vs mountains vs foreground vs river
chalk bluffs as a scene feature
left-side light as a compositional driver
sections.description: The speaker identifies four zones in the frame, notes unequal illumination (left-side mountains brighter), and frames the task of balancing light across sky, mountains, and foreground. Chalk bluffs are mentioned as an unwanted element to be managed.

sections.title: Sky extension and initial haze planning
sections.description: Plan to deepen the sky, shift light direction, and prepare to extend clouds to frame edges. The left-side light becomes the primary light source to be emphasized across edits.

sections.title: Layer separation and initial light shaping
sections.description: Emphasis on separating layers as the foundational workflow. The speaker adjusts exposure and whites in RAW, warms the highlights, and begins crafting light to the mountains, setting up for additive color and light painting.

sections.title: Midground and foreground refinement
concepts: color bleed via painting rather than strict selections
cloud texture and foreground texture management
sections.description: Midground and foreground are refined; river brightness is increased to guide eye flow, and color is allowed to bleed between areas to create a cohesive, painterly look. Small brush work starts to shape light across elements.

sections.title: Texture, HDR-like cloud detail, and early luminosity work
sections.description: Texture enhancement of clouds via auto HDR and sponge-like edits, plus early uses of blur and luminosity to push depth. The instructor emphasizes maintaining separation between layers to preserve depth cues.

sections.title: Background completion and composition adjustments
concepts: warp tool to reduce distracting elements
sections.description: Further separation of background elements, inserting a brighter, warmer background sky where appropriate, and using warp to tame a distracting bush without cutting it out entirely. The goal is a believable multi-layer scene.

sections.title: Color control and selective color experiments
sections.description: The tutorial delves into selective color and the 50-150 adjustment tool to intensify mountain reds/yellows and push other colors, while carefully avoiding haloing and maintaining three-dimensional separation. The presenter explains the relationship between color, saturation, and luminance in this context.

sections.title: Recap, final tweaks, and closing thoughts
concepts: final balance between blacks and perceived depth
benefits of painting light over relying on captured light
sections.description: The closing section reinforces the key workflow: extend sky, separate layers, paint light, apply blur + luminosity, and preserve blacks for depth. The speaker emphasizes painting light rather than depending solely on captured light for dramatic effect.

featured_techniques.technique: Sky extension using duplicate sky and clone stamp
Painting light onto mountains with brush
Blur plus luminosity to create atmospheric glow
Warp tool to remove a distracting foreground element while preserving composition
Auto HDR and texture enhancement for clouds
Selective color and color grading for tonal separation
